newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia c.bank offers plan on frozen MinFin bonds.
newsitem.headline: Russia c.bank offers plan on frozen MinFin bonds.

text.p: Russia needs to change the registration and depositary system for MinFin bonds to overcome the problem which has arosen with frozen bonds, a central bank official said on Tuesday.
At present the bonds are in bearer form, and an investor depositing them at a depositary has the right to withdraw the same bonds with the same serial numbers as he deposited.

Switching to a system of "depersonalised" bonds, in which depositaries only record what volume of bonds an investor has, not the serial numbers, would make it impossible for the authorities to freeze individual stolen or missing bonds.

Earlier this year the authorities froze $24.22 million of the dollar-denominated bonds, which had gone missing. Banking sources said in late August an order to freeze up to a further $7 million nominal of MinFin bonds was being prepared.

"We are helping Vneshtorgbank (a major MinFin bond depositary) to organise depersonalised accounting," said Dmitry Budakov, head of the central bank's department for control of bank activities on financial markets.

"If this scheme is adopted, the problems will be resolved at least for those who agree to depersonalised accounting," Budakov said. The central bank had informed the finance ministry about the plan, he said.
He said another step was to persuade the prosecutor general and arbitration court that the bonds had been frozen in contravention of the civil code.
Russia's civil code states that bearer bonds cannot be withdrawn from those who bought them in good faith.
